items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: I got my Aunt Edna B. Saunders to teach me the words to a song... that's the first time anyone taught me anything about dancing besides my Aunt Edna B. Saunders

ctx.x: Well, I was about -- I was little. I was only seven years old then. And she says, 'Would you like that? I say, 'Yes, ma'am.' So she says, 'Have you ever worked in a theater before? And I say, 'Why no, ma'am, I haven't.' I say, 'I've been on the radio. I worked for the American Broadcasting Company on Children's Hour.'

She say, 'Well, what you should do is go in the theater there on the amateur show and get in the amateur show and go on stage, said, your mother would like that. It would be a nice surprise for your mother when she come. So I say, 'Yes, ma'am, say, how would I do that?' She say, 'Well, just -- you just come to the theater and come backstage, go to the box office there and tell them at the box office you would like to be one of the amateurs in the amateur show.'
